newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Ceramco sees slow rebound, enough for div.
newsitem.headline: Ceramco sees slow rebound, enough for div.

text.p: New Zealand diversified manufacturer Ceramco Corporation Limited said on Wednesday that after reporting an unsatisfactory full-year result it nevertheless expected improvements and a sufficient level of earnings in 1997/98 to enable it to continue to pay dividends.
Its struggling apparel division, in the midst of a strategic improvement plan, would take 12 months "to significantly contribute to earnings", it added in a statement.
"Further sales of surplus assets are currently being negotiated and these will enhance cashflow," Ceramco said.
"Overall the 1997/98 year should see earnings before tax and non-recurring items at a level which will enable continuation of the payment of dividends to shareholders," it added.

The company is in the midst of looking for a new chief executive officer for its Bendon Hickory lingerie unit but said the search had been difficult and "discussions are currently being held with prospective candidates".
It said that its NZ China Clays operation was budgeted to improve on this year's result in 1997/98 and its Klipper and John Webster units were also due to contribute to profits.

Ceramco returned a net profit for the year to March of just NZ$0.96 million, down a massive 91 percent from the year-ago level of $11.3 million. However, on the basis of a good cash position and what the directors called "a very strong balance sheet" it paid a final dividend of 7.5 cents, having opted not to pay an interim dividend at the half-year point.
This gave a total of 7.5 cents, versus 17.5 a year ago.
